beats.en: Dhara wants to give 18 laddoos equally to 9 people. She gives one to each person, then another, and checks how many are left. After two rounds nothing is left, so each person gets 2. We write 18 ÷ 9 = 2.
beats.speakEn: Dhara wants to give 18 laddoos equally to 9 people. She gives one to each person, then another, and checks how many are left. After two rounds nothing is left, so each person gets 2. We write 18  divided by  9  equals  2.

Rule: Dhara wants to give 18 laddoos equally to 9 people.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · Raksha Bandhan · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: On a number track, Dhara jumps from 0 by 3 each time. She lands on 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on. Skip jumping is repeated addition.

beats.en: On a number track, Dhara jumps from 0 by 3 each time. She lands on 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on. Skip jumping is repeated addition. After 1 jump she is at 3, after 2 jumps at 6 = 2 × 3 and after 3 jumps at 9 = 3 × 3.
beats.speakEn: On a number track, Dhara jumps from 0 by 3 each time. She lands on 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on. Skip jumping is repeated addition. After 1 jump she is at 3, after 2 jumps at 6  equals  2  times  3 and after 3 jumps at 9  equals  3  times  3.

beats.en: If 4 jalebis are given to each of 9 people, we need 9 × 4 = 36 jalebis. 24 jalebis are not enough. To buy enough jalebis for 9 people, Dhara should buy 36, so she needs 12 more.
beats.speakEn: If 4 jalebis are given to each of 9 people, we need 9  times  4  equals  36 jalebis. 24 jalebis are not enough. To buy enough jalebis for 9 people, Dhara should buy 36, so she needs 12 more.

type: On a number track, Dhara jumps from 0 by 3 each time. She lands on 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on.
If 4 jalebis are given to each of 9 people, we need 9 × 4 = 36 jalebis. 24 jalebis are not enough.
